mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in liquidity and an increase in borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over the previous quarter indicates a contraction in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 declines > 1% QoQ, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases > 2% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signals disinflationary pressures, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when CPIAUCSL decreases for 3 consecutive months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200k, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is increasing and real final sales (RSAFS) are decreasing, it signals a supply-side mismatch, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases and RSAFS decreases, the hypothesis is rejected.
